sources.summary:
Engineer Venkatesh Rao compares the fear of AI job losses to mercantilism: intelligence is treated as a scarce resource that elites want to control. But AI could boost demand for human thinking, much like early capitalism made people voluntarily work more.

en.title: Tencent releases Hyra 2.0, and AutoResearch, AI's foray into scientific research, has entered its second half too—shifting from gacha-style problem grinding to tooling upgrades.
en.summary:
Tencent has released Hyra 2.0, and AI-driven scientific research platform AutoResearch has entered its second half, shifting from lucky-draw trial and error to tooling upgrades.

Put simply, Hyra 2.0 builds a hardcore Harness — an agent engineering foundation.

Agents can plug directly into WeCom to ask humans to approve compute, and internally advance asynchronously across three layers: Overall (global oversight), Mission (route planning) and Worker (running experiments).

It also introduces a Review Worker with an independent context that can inspect raw code and logs directly and feed lessons learned into a shared knowledge base, automatically distilling them into reusable Skills during retrospectives.

It has already produced a series of results:

en.title: Oh, right, our team also has 2 AI Engineer headcount openings, also Work From Home friendly.
en.summary:
Oh, and one more thing — our team has 2 more AI Engineer headcount, also Work From Home friendly. 🏠

Unlike DeepSeek Harness, which focuses on 2–10 years of experience, we'd rather have 10+ year veterans and architects who still love writing code. 😄

After all, an Agent can write code on its own, but when something breaks in production, you still need a few grizzled engineers who've been through the trenches to backstop it. 😂

We're looking for people with hands-on Coding Agent experience, familiar with Claude Code, Skills, Hooks, MCP, and Agent Runtime, and still willing to get in there and write code themselves.

Let's build Agent products that actually run reliably inside enterprise engineering workflows — not just demos.

Resumes welcome…
en.reason: Two AI Engineer HC roles with Work From Home target 10+ year coders and architects—not DeepSeek Harness's 2–10 years—who know Claude Code, Hooks and MCP and want to build Agent products that run stably in enterprise workflows, not demos.

sources.title_original: Is OpenAI Having Trouble Raising Money?
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 据Financial Times报道，OpenAI把本轮融资目标从约300亿美元下调至200亿美元、估值从1.4万亿美元降至1.25万亿美元，文章指出这是AI重定价首次直接波及私营前沿实验室。

en.reason: OpenAI cut its funding target from about $30 billion to $20 billion and its valuation from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion, per the Financial Times, amid the first AI repricing to directly affect a private frontier lab.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章介绍 NVIDIA AICR 如何用可复用 recipe 简化 Kubernetes 对 Vera Rubin 的配置，并在 GPU Operator v26.7.0、DRA driver v0.5.0 与 R615 驱动上完成训练和推理端到端验证，还记录早期硬件 fabric 故障及恢复。

en.reason: NVIDIA AICR's reusable recipes simplify Kubernetes configuration for Vera Rubin, with end-to-end training and inference validated on GPU Operator v26.7.0, DRA driver v0.5.0 and R615 drivers, plus documented early fabric failures and recovery.

stories.title: 10.26—11.1｜本周精选 AI 论文

sources.title: 10.26—11.1｜本周精选 AI 论文
sources.title_zh: 10.26—11.1｜本周精选 AI 论文
sources.title_original: 10.26—11.1｜本周精选 AI 论文
sources.summary: 这一周的精选 AI论文有个很明显的信号：AI 系统开始从“把更强模型塞进更多 Agent”，转向让检索、验证、记忆和模型协作各自做更确定的事。想把 Agent 做稳的人，这批研究比单纯看模型榜单更有参考价值。
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 本期精选涵盖DecisionRAG与Unified Training：前者用决策模型逐层检索，在MultiDoc2Dial上R@1较密集检索加8B重排序器高13.8点，单次查询耗时0.7至1.8秒；后者把预训练到强化学习置于单一似然算法下。

en.title: 10.26–11.1 | This Week's Best AI Papers
en.summary: This week's curated AI papers send a clear signal: AI systems are moving away from "stuffing stronger models into more Agents" and toward making retrieval, verification, memory, and model collaboration each do more deterministic work. For anyone trying to build Agents that hold up, these studies are more useful than simply scanning model leaderboards.
en.reason: DecisionRAG's decision-model layered retrieval beats dense retrieval plus an 8B reranker by 13.8 R@1 points on MultiDoc2Dial at 0.7–1.8 seconds per query, while Unified Training unifies pretraining through RL under one likelihood algorithm in this week's selected AI papers.

sources.title_zh: ChatGPT 12月合并额度：以后提问还得先打草稿？
sources.title_original: ChatGPT 12月合并额度：以后提问还得先打草稿？
sources.summary: OpenAI 在12月份的额度新规牵动了不少重度用户：ChatGPT高级对话与Codex将共用Token池，仅Instant快速对话不计入额度。作者的真实体验帮你提前看清订阅成本变化，看懂和Claude体系一样的计费逻辑，避免后续想用强推理模型时束手束脚。
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 12月起Plus、Pro和Business用户的ChatGPT与Codex共用Token额度，Instant聊天不扣；Chat与Work界面将小范围测试合并。

en.title: ChatGPT's December quota merge: will we have to draft our prompts before asking?
en.summary: OpenAI's new December quota rules have rattled plenty of heavy users: advanced ChatGPT conversations and Codex will share a single Token pool, with only Instant quick chats exempt from the quota. The author's firsthand experience offers an early look at how subscription costs will shift, and decodes billing logic that mirrors Claude's — so you won't find your hands tied later when you want to use strong reasoning models.
en.reason: From December, OpenAI will make Plus, Pro and Business users share one Token pool across ChatGPT advanced conversations and Codex, with Instant chats exempt, and a hands-on account shows how subscription costs and strong-reasoning access change.

stories.title: 最近我一直在琢磨一个事儿：AI Agent 到底还能怎么卷？ 看了一圈各路大模型的更新，天天都在卷参数、卷推理速度、卷谁更聪明。 但说实话， @termix_ai 光停留在“帮人类写写代码、做做表格”这个层面，想象空间其实已经被压得很窄了。 真正的分水岭，绝对不是看它能帮人类打多少工，而是看它什么时候能自己支棱起来，变成一个独立的、能赚钱的商业个体。 这几天关注到搞的方向，刚好戳中了这个点。 从“打工人”到“老板”，AI 的角色变了…

en.title: Lately I've been thinking about one thing: how much further can the AI Agent race go?
en.summary:
I keep coming back to one question: how much further can AI Agents actually be pushed?

Looking across the major model updates, it is the same race every day—parameters, inference speed, who is smarter.

But honestly, with @termix_ai still stuck at helping humans write code and build spreadsheets, the room for imagination has already been squeezed pretty narrow.

The real dividing line is definitely not how much work it can do for humans, but when it can stand on its own and become an independent, revenue-generating business entity.

The direction I have been watching these past few days hits exactly that point.

From employee to boss: AI's role is changing
Over the past year, expectations for AI have largely remained that of a useful tool.

It does whatever you ask, and you still have to pay its API fees when you are done. But TermiX's logic is a little different—it wants to...
en.reason: TermiX is pushing AI agents beyond writing code and making spreadsheets toward becoming independent, profit-earning business entities, framing autonomy—not parameter or inference-speed races—as the real dividing line for the technology.

en.title: When CI breaks, who's the gatekeeper? Buildkite's new agent approach
en.reason: Buildkite now scopes secrets to a single pipeline with authorization by branch, queue, source or creator, and ships MCP tools such as validate_pipeline and compare_builds so agents can check YAML, diagnose failed builds and repair webhooks.

en.title: 🚨 Has the Scaling Law Really Stopped Working?
en.summary:
🚨 Has Scaling Law really stopped working? I actually think AI is entering a brand-new Scaling phase.

Over the past few years, almost all AI progress has depended on Scaling Law.

But many people misunderstand it, thinking Scaling simply means endlessly stacking parameters.

In fact, the core of Scaling Law is studying the predictable relationship between compute resources and model performance.

Looking back at AI’s development, four major stages stand out.

1️⃣ Pre-training Scaling: scaling up

In 2020, OpenAI’s Kaplan et al. found an empirical power-law relationship between language model Loss and parameter count, data volume, and training compute.

This has gradually turned large-model training from empirical exploration into a…
en.reason: OpenAI's Kaplan and colleagues showed in 2020 that language-model loss follows an empirical power law with parameters, data and training compute, supporting an argument that Scaling Law is not dead but entering a new stage beyond parameter stacking.

en.title: 🚨 Has the Scaling Law Really Stopped Working?
en.summary:
🚨 Has Scaling Law really stopped working? I actually think AI is entering a brand-new Scaling phase.

Over the past few years, almost all AI progress has depended on Scaling Law.

But many people misunderstand it, thinking Scaling simply means endlessly stacking parameters.

In fact, the core of Scaling Law is studying the predictable relationship between compute resources and model performance.

Looking back at AI’s development, four major stages stand out.

1️⃣ Pre-training Scaling: scaling up

In 2020, OpenAI’s Kaplan et al. found an empirical power-law relationship between language model Loss and parameter count, data volume, and training compute.

en.reason: OpenAI's Kaplan and colleagues showed in 2020 that language-model loss follows an empirical power law with parameters, data and training compute, supporting an argument that Scaling Law is not dead but entering a new stage beyond parameter stacking.

en.title: Damn, this is a rock-solid topic-picking assistant!
en.summary:
Holy crap, this is a killer topic-picking assistant!!

The most time-consuming part of finding topics every day is bouncing between apps scrolling hot lists. The open-source project TrendRadar turns that into a briefing pushed to your phone on a schedule.

What it does (per the README):
· Aggregates hot lists and RSS from multiple platforms, with keyword filtering
· AI filtering: write what you care about in plain language in ai_interests.txt, and the AI scores every story, pushing only the relevant ones
· AI translation and briefing analysis
· Pushes to Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, Telegram, email and other channels
· MCP support, so you can ask it about trends in natural language

Which accounts can use it right away:
· Trend-chasing creators: a hot topic lands on your phone the moment it hits the list, so you can publish before you'd even spot it by scrolling apps
· Cross-platform…

en.title: In the first round of testing, I gave each of them the screenshot from the original tweet and asked them to find the highest-resolution version of that wallpaper. Here are the results (the images also show each Agent's result in the order listed): 1.
en.summary:
In the first round of testing, I gave each of them the screenshots from the original tweet and asked them to find the highest-resolution version of the wallpaper. The results were as follows (the images are also shown in the order of the text for each Agent's result):

1. Grok bot: Found the original image on Twitter fastest, but it was only 736×736, so it returned that and stopped.
2. Muse: Searched for a very long time, browsed many pages, and had me approve many permissions before ultimately returning the same 736×736 image. It said it actually knew there was a 1024×1024 image online but simply couldn't download it.
3. Cue: Didn't find it at all and gave up. It even blamed me for not cropping out the icons from other apps in the screenshot.
4. Comma: Searched for quite a while and in the end only found that 736... one on Twitter.
en.reason: Four agents given the same screenshot to find a wallpaper's highest-resolution version: Grok bot returned fastest but only at 736×736, Muse knew of a 1024×1024 file yet couldn't download it, and Cue gave up entirely.

en.summary:
In the first round of testing, I gave each of them the screenshots from the original tweet and asked them to find the highest-resolution version of the wallpaper. The results were as follows (the images are also shown in the order of the text for each Agent's result):

1. Grok bot: Found the original image on Twitter fastest, but it was only 736×736, so it returned that and stopped.
2. Muse: Searched for a very long time, browsed many pages, and had me approve many permissions before ultimately returning the same 736×736 image. It said it actually knew there was a 1024×1024 image online but simply couldn't download it.
3. Cue: Didn't find it at all and gave up. It even blamed me for not cropping out the icons from other apps in the screenshot.
4. Comma: Searched for quite a while and in the end only found that 736... one on Twitter.
en.reason: Four agents given the same screenshot to find a wallpaper's highest-resolution version: Grok bot returned fastest but only at 736×736, Muse knew of a 1024×1024 file yet couldn't download it, and Cue gave up entirely.

en.title: Unbelievable — now even an Alibaba VP is doing livestream selling?
en.summary:
Unbelievable — Alibaba's vice president is doing livestream selling too??

At 7:30 tonight, "Token" will go on sale in Li Jiaqi's Tmall Double 11 livestream, and 200 trillion Tokens will be handed out in the stream.

The livestream targets a female audience, themed "The AI Office Buddy for Every Girl."

Besides Token, the stream will showcase a range of AI office products and AI hardware. Alibaba vice president Chen Yusen will appear as a guest.

Public records show Chen Yusen was born in 1992 — the same age as Li Jiaqi — and is Alibaba's youngest vice president.

In June this year, Alibaba announced a DingTalk management reshuffle: founder Chen Hang (nickname Wu Zhao) stepped down as DingTalk CEO, with Chen Yusen taking over.

In July, Alibaba brought together the programmable agent app QoderWork, the AI work platform Wukong and MuleRun — three AI Age…

sources.title_original: 科普下 AI 降智
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章拆解“降智”的真实成因：中转站页面挂着 Opus、GPT 背后偷偷降级，Fable 5 回退 Opus 4.8，1M 上下文过满触发压缩、并发限流，并给出两个 100 刀 codex 账号优于一个 200 刀的实操建议。

en.title: A quick explainer on AI getting dumber
en.reason: Model downgrading isn't one failure: relay sites display Opus or GPT while silently downgrading the real model, Fable 5 falls back to Opus 4.8, a full 1M context triggers compression—so two $100 Codex accounts can beat one $200.

en.title: EMBRACE attack breaks through the browsers of five AI coding tools, making local dev machines the biggest attack surface
en.reason: Forever Security's Gal Weizman showed EMBRACE flaws in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code and Claude Desktop, where preview browsers let websites run commands or local HTML steal SSH keys, affecting over 45 million.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: 作者用微信小程序和零第三方依赖的Node.js做病历归档，实测本地Ollama跑Qwen2.5-VL 3B识别一张病历需40-60秒，撞上wx.request的60秒硬上限，只能改成异步任务加1.2秒轮询。

en.title: I built a medical records archiving mini-program and got a harsh lesson in the "last mile" of AI recognition
en.reason: A WeChat mini-program for archiving medical records pairs a native frontend with a zero-dependency Node.js backend, and its local Ollama Qwen2.5-VL 3B recognition takes 40–60 seconds per image, forcing async tasks plus 1.2-second polling under wx.request’s 60-second limit.

stories.title: AI眼镜能替代你的近视眼镜，但真的应该吗？ / AI glasses can replace your prescription glasses, but should they?

sources.title_zh: AI眼镜能替代你的近视眼镜，但真的应该吗？

sources.title_original: AI glasses can replace your prescription glasses, but should they?
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章探讨AI glasses能否替代日常处方眼镜：Ray-Ban Meta可上传处方配镜，但智能眼镜重达80克、续航仅3到5小时，且英格兰和威尔士法院及纽约7月已禁用Meta glasses，隐私与全天佩戴是主要顾虑。

en.reason: Ray-Ban Meta can be fitted with prescription lenses, but at 80 grams and 3–5 hours of battery life, AI glasses face privacy concerns and bans on Meta glasses in England and Wales courts and New York in July.
